children: Benchmark paused just below its peak as semiconductor gains offset weakness in banks and consumer platforms. Asia extended its rally, oil fell below $100 and the dollar reached a two-month high.
Index looks calm, market underneath does not

The S&P 500 finished virtually unchanged at 7,764.64 Tuesday, remaining less than 0.5% below its August record. The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.45% to a second consecutive record close, while the Dow fell 0.36%. S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were steady Wednesday morning.
Market breadth was mixed, with six of the S&P 500’s 11 sectors declining. Financials dropped 1.7%, while JPMorgan and Wells Fargo each lost more than 3%.
Trading volume reached 17.9 billion shares, above the 20-day average of 16.3 billion, so the reshuffling was hardly casual.
The S&P’s immediate test remains the August record area, while the 7,700 region provides the first meaningful buffer beneath the market.
A breakout supported by broader participation would carry more weight than another tech-led advance accompanied by weakness across banks, transport and consumer platforms.
AI creates winners — and losers

Micron rallied 5% and Sandisk gained almost 7% as the AI trade rotated into memory and storage. Semiconductor shares have now advanced for six consecutive sessions, reflecting expectations that AI agents will require more processors, memory capacity and data-center infrastructure as consumer adoption expands.
The same technology created a less flattering group of movers. Charles Schwab dropped 6.1%, Airbnb lost 3% and Uber and Lyft fell more than 1% as investors considered whether AI agents like
could eventually handle brokerage, travel and shopping tasks that currently send customers through established platforms.

Meta Connect begins Wednesday, with Mark Zuckerberg’s keynote scheduled for 7 p.m. ET. Options markets imply a move of approximately 4.5% in either direction by Friday. Traders want evidence that Muse’s strong download figures can translate into retention, subscriptions, commerce and advertising revenue.
Asia rises as oil and yields offer relief

Asian equities headed for a sixth consecutive advance. MSCI’s regional index gained 0.7%, South Korea’s Kospi climbed 1.2% and Taiwan added 0.9%. Samsung and SK Hynix rose more than 2%. Japan remained closed, although Nikkei futures traded almost 2,000 points above Friday’s cash close.

Brent crude slipped to roughly $99.20 and US oil fell toward $90 after Saudi Arabia restarted its East–West Pipeline. Markets are also watching for possible US-Iran discussions as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addresses the UN.

The 10-year Treasury yield stayed below 5%, but the two-year yield reached 4.79%, its highest since mid-2024. Traders assign roughly a 54% probability to another Fed hike in October. The dollar index rose toward a two-month high, with EUR/USD near $1.1440 and USD/JPY around ¥157.60.
Gold stalls while Bitcoin holds its breakout

Gold eased toward $4,340 as higher short-term yields and a stronger dollar outweighed geopolitical demand. Copper moved closer to record territory after gaining roughly 18% this year, supported by constrained supply and expectations for heavy investment in power networks, data centers and AI infrastructure.
Bitcoin held around $86,700 after briefly trading above $87,000. The OG coin remains well above the
that rejected rallies in May and early September.

Xi Jinping’s arrival in Washington provides the next cross-market catalyst. Thursday’s meeting with Trump could cover trade, tariffs, AI regulation, supply chains and the Iran conflict. An extended trade truce would support equities and industrial metals; renewed friction would quickly test the S&P 500’s calm exterior.
S&P 500 flat below all-time high
AI rally rotates into memory chips
Asian equities back at it again

title: SPX: S&P 500 Holds Near Record as AI Rally Narrows. Futures Tick Higher.
